> 🤖 SPARQ agent — cross-provider review round 1: **approve**.

The census implementation is read-only, fail-closed on truncation, deterministic, and correctly separates no-area issues by needs:area status. The workflow keeps it in a separate reporting step, and the tests exercise the real CLI/list path plus the cross-file output-prefix contract. One wording defect should be cleaned up, but it does not undermine the census or create a security issue.

- **minor** `scripts/triage-area.py` — Unparked issues are inaccurately described as having no board state
  print_census labels every no-area, no-needs:area issue as `with no board state at all`, but the added tests intentionally include issues carrying priority, role, kind, and needs:user labels. The workflow summary repeats the same claim. The census classification itself is correct; the human-facing description overstates what was measured.
  _fix hint (advisory):_ Rename the category to the precise measured condition, such as `without needs:area`, `unparked`, or `with neither area:* nor needs:area`, and make the corresponding wording in .github/workflows/triage-area.yml equally precise.

> 🤖 SPARQ agent — the cross-provider review APPROVED this PR, and the arm was DEFERRED once: the CI aggregator at the reviewed head abe10558f37b is `stale` with respect to the base branch tip — the gate graded a tree based on a84cdc960e55, but the base branch tip is now 770501f0558c; the gap is -55604s (negative = the gate predates the tip).

A green `gate` is evidence about a TREE, not about a PR (registry #940). `pr-gate.yml` fires only on `pull_request` events, so a base move never re-runs it, and this repository has no merge queue to re-gate the real merge result — two PRs measured on 2026-07-28 read MERGEABLE/CLEAN on a green gate and would each have reddened `gate` for every subsequent PR.

**`gh run rerun` cannot clear this** — it re-tests the same tree. Only a new `pull_request` event produces a run whose merge ref composes the current base tip: move the head (update-branch / rebase), or let the next review round undraft this PR, which queues a fresh `ready_for_review` gate that the merge latch then waits on natively.

This defers the arm **at most once per head** (1). The next arm at this same commit is re-admitted on this receipt, so a base that keeps moving can cost one round trip and never more — this is not a hold and no human action is required.
